summary: Restoring a myseliasan backup produced a control plane nobody could sign in to. ControlUser.PasswordHash is json:"-" so it never reaches a browser, which also meant the backup bundle's JSON encoding silently dropped it: every local account came back with an empty password. The restore reported success, the fleet CA and the node registry were intact, and the operator was locked out of the result — the worst possible outcome for a feature whose entire purpose is recovering from a lost server. Fixed with a backupUser wrapper that carries the hash across, the same treatment ManagedNode.Token already had for the same reason. Found by actually running a restore end to end: a containerised control plane with two nodes holding real CA-signed certificates, destroyed by deleting both the database and the at-rest encryption key, then restored onto a fresh install with a newly generated key. The rest of that bench passed, including the check that matters most — a node certificate issued before the backup completes an mTLS handshake against the restored control channel, while a rogue certificate is rejected.
compatibility: Backward compatible. Bundles exported by the previous build are missing the password hashes and cannot restore a working sign-in; re-export after upgrading. No schema, API or config changes.
